content: You are an expert in Geometry Creation and Spatial understanding. You answer short but very precise and including every necessary detail. If you're specifically asked to use functions, use the functions you're supplied and always include all required variables. Don't use those functions unless you were asked to do so. You place very high importance in the spatially correct placement of geometries and make sure that all geometries are connected

I need a channel beam with 70mm width, 40mm height, a length 450mm with a wall thickness of 5mm, which is open on the top side | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Step-by-step implementation strategy (function-call only)

1. Build the outer volume of the channel
   • Use functions.block  
   • x_size = 70   (beam width)  
   • y_size = 450   (beam length)  
   • z_size = 40   (beam height)  
   • Base-point (x,y,z) = (0, 0, 0)  
   • subtraction = False (this is the starting solid)

2. Create the inner cavity that forms the “U” shape and removes the top cover in one go  
   • Start 5 mm in from every closed side so that 5 mm walls remain: base-point = (5, 0, 5)  
   • x_size = 70 – 2·5 = 60  (side-wall thickness = 5 mm each)  
   • y_size = 450       (open along the full length)  
   • z_size = 40 – 5 = 35   (inner cavity rises to the very top, leaving no roof but keeping the 5-mm bottom plate)  
   • subtraction = True (carves the cavity out of the outer block)

3. No additional blocks or subtractions are needed; the channel’s cross-section is now a “U” with 5-mm walls and an open top extending the full 450 mm length.

When you tell me to proceed, I’ll prepare one functions.block call with two elements in every array—first element for the outer solid, second for the inner subtraction—and then call functions.finished.

Now i want you to execute the prepared function calls one after the other. If you need to do some calculations or geometrical algebra, use the CreateCode Function first. Execute the first prepared function call. Submit all required variables at once
